claims.quote: 10 महीने में 14 बार दो-दो चुनाव आयुक्तों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त से असहमति जाहिर की है।
claims.translation: In 10 months, two Election Commissioners have expressed disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner 14 times.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: The Indian Express investigation of 23 Sep 2026 (Ritika Chopra; he also names Damini Nath).
claims.check: The count of 14 matches the Express. The framing differs slightly: the Express says the objections were to 'decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge', copied to the CEC, not disagreements with the CEC as such.
claims.site_counts: The process page's 'Inside the Commission' section lists the dated objections from the Express special issue and keeps the paper's own count (14) in prose; it is press, not a document the site has seen.
claims.site_stops: The site has not seen the notes; it can only say what the Express reports.

claims.quote: नमस्कार, मैं रवश कुमार। वोट चोरी का सिस्टम पकड़ा गया है। यह सिस्टम कहीं और नहीं चुनाव आयोग के भीतर पकड़ा गया है।
claims.translation: The system of vote theft has been caught. It has been caught nowhere else but inside the Election Commission.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: The Express report, read together with Rahul Gandhi's 2025 press conferences, which the episode plays at length.
claims.check: The Express reports objections about process, access to the roll software, Form 6 and appeals, and says of West Bengal: 'There was no evidence of its role in the election outcome.' It does not report vote theft.
claims.site_counts: Nothing on the site measures intent; its rule is that the lists cannot show intent.
claims.site_stops: The site does not and cannot say whether anything was stolen.

claims.quote: 97 लोगों ने साबित कर दिया कि वोटर लिस्ट में उनका नाम होना चाहिए ... जिस अधिकारी के सामने दावा किया वो मान भी गया लेकिन दिल्ली से कंट्रोल हो रहा सॉफ्टवेयर उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट में नहीं जोड़ता है।
claims.translation: 97 people proved they should be on the roll ... the officer accepted their claim, but the software controlled from Delhi did not add them.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: The Express Goa report (Goa CEO's office wrote eight times, 11-17 Feb 2026).
claims.check: Matches the Express account.
claims.site_counts: The process page carries the Goa sequence (11 to 21 Feb 2026) from the Express special issue, labelled press. Goa's own figures (1,00,042 left off the draft, 8.44 per 100) are in the All India table.
claims.site_stops: The 97 are the paper's count; the site has no list of them.

claims.quote: मीडिया ने भी 13 करोड़ लोगों का चेहरा गायब कर दिया।
claims.translation: The media too made the faces of 13 crore people disappear.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: The 13 crore draft-stage total (Express, 1 Sep 2026).
claims.check: The figure is right as a sum of draft-stage removals; the site's own sum across 32 states and UTs is 13,39,03,307. It counts names left off draft rolls, which includes the dead and duplicates and is before any restoration, so it is not 13 crore people disenfranchised.
claims.site_counts: All India: 13.39 crore names left off the drafts, about a fifth (20.8%) entered as dead in the states whose split by reason is complete; final rolls are above the draft in several states.
claims.site_stops: The site cannot say how many of the 13 crore were eligible electors.

claims.quote: पश्चिम बंगाल में 27 लाख वोटरों को चुनाव में वोट देने का मौका नहीं मिला।
claims.translation: In West Bengal, 27 lakh voters did not get the chance to vote in the election.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: The Commission's adjudication outcome in West Bengal (as reported).
claims.check: Matches the reported adjudication split: 27,16,393 found not eligible of 60,06,675 held for adjudication.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal page: 27,16,393 found not eligible, 32,68,119 found eligible, 37,05,235 appeals pending as reported (22,21,118 by the excluded, 16,10,311 against inclusion). Only 1,607 were restored before the poll.
claims.site_stops: These are state totals as reported; the site cannot say how many of the 27 lakh were eligible, because 96.7% of appeals were still pending.

claims.quote: 20 अगस्त से 24 सितंबर के बीच 29,000 से ज्यादा फॉर्म सेवन भरे गए हैं। इनमें से 93% आम लोगों ने भरे हैं।
claims.translation: Between 20 August and 24 September more than 29,000 Form 7s were filed [in Karnataka], 93% of them by ordinary people.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: A Karnataka minister's letter to the state CEO (he names Arshad Rizwan); the Belagavi account is from The Hindu.
claims.check: Not verified: the figure is the minister's, relayed; the CEO's own count was not found. The minister is a party office-holder.
claims.site_counts: The Disputes page lists bulk Form 7 objections with their sources; Karnataka's own pages carry district figures from the CEO only.
claims.site_stops: The site holds no CEO count of Form 7s by who filed them.

claims.quote: नए वोटर और बहुत से पुराने वोटर के लिए इसका प्रमाण देना मुश्किल होने लगा और उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट से कटने लगा।
claims.translation: For new voters and many old ones, proving this became difficult and their names began to be struck off the roll.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the runtime; treat as +/- 1 to 2 minutes
claims.relies_on: His reading of the Form 6 declaration change.
claims.check: Form 6 is the application for new enrolment; the declaration could delay or block an application, but no source found shows it removing existing names. The Express says applicants could not submit without answering it.
claims.site_counts: The process page's Form 6 section sets out the declaration and the Commissioners' objections from documents and the Express.
claims.site_stops: No count exists of Form 6 applications refused because of the declaration.

strongest_points: He follows and relays the Express documents closely (14 objections, Goa's 97, ERO access to ERONet), and the West Bengal adjudication figure he uses (27 lakh) is the reported official one.
He relays a Bombay High Court bench's remarks on Goa (Form 8 rejected because the software could not restore an EPIC), which are about process and are checkable.
overreach: Moves from the Express's process findings to 'vote theft' and 'democracy looted', which the Express itself does not claim.
Mixes in long clips of the Leader of the Opposition, so the episode's claims are not always his own; claims made only in those clips are excluded here.
Treats the 13 crore draft-stage total as people erased.
not_verified: The Karnataka Form 7 figures (29,000; 93%; 4,700 in three days) are a minister's, not checked against the CEO.
No written piece by him on the SIR in 2025-26 was located; only these two videos were opened. Earlier Bihar-era episodes were not reachable from the channel page (it lists only the latest 30).

claims.quote: a good electoral roll of Bihar should have 8 crore 18 lakh people, but it had 7.9 crores. So there was deficit of 29 lakhs to begin with
claims.relies_on: Census-based projection of Bihar's adult population (Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections) against the January 2025 roll.
claims.check: Quoted as reported by LiveLaw.
claims.site_counts: The site uses the same projection family: about 8.30 crore adults projected for 1 March 2026 against a roll of 7.90 crore before the revision (the Commission's June 2025 total, 7,89,69,844) and 7.24 crore on the draft. Across 19 states, rolls held 98.3% of projected adults before and 84.4% after the drafts.
claims.site_stops: Projections count residents, so a state that sends migrants out counts adults who may be registered at home; the site says so beside the figure.

claims.quote: Total eligible adults: The government report projects Bihar's 18+ population in July 2025 at 8.18 crore ... New registered voters: The ECI's press release states that the new draft roll contains only 7.24 crore voters. The shortfall: 8.18 crore – 7.24 crore = 94 lakh.
claims.speaker_note: The Wire's text, presenting Yadav's calculation.
claims.relies_on: Technical Group population projection; ECI draft-roll press note.
claims.check: Arithmetic checks. Elector-population ratio 97% before and 88% after, as stated.
claims.site_counts: Same direction on the site's numbers: draft 7,24,05,756; phase 1 removals 65,59,409 in the booth file (65,59,626 in the lists).
claims.site_stops: The site does not call the gap 'disenfranchised': part of it is new 18-year-olds not yet enrolled and part is the projection's own error.

claims.quote: 25 lakh men and 31 lakh women have been deleted
claims.relies_on: ECI draft-stage deletion data by sex (as he presented it).
claims.check: Close to the site's own count; the reasoning attached (more men migrate and die) is his inference.
claims.site_counts: Bihar phase 1: women 55.5% of names removed against 47.9% of the roll; over-represented in all 38 districts (by 2.8 to 13.7 points) and 242 of 243 seats. Entered as dead: 52.0% women against 43.4% of expected adult deaths (SRS).
claims.site_stops: The lists cannot say why; marriage moves explain about half a year's worth of the excess and the district pattern runs the other way.

claims.quote: Never in the history of this country has any revision ever asked all people to submit a form or to submit a document. NEVER
claims.relies_on: His reading of the 2003 intensive revision.
claims.check: Not verified here against the 2003 order, which he said was not public.
claims.site_counts: The process page sets out the 2025 order's form and document requirement from the documents.
claims.site_stops: The site has not compared the 2003 instructions.

claims.quote: We are witnessing perhaps the largest exercise of disenfranchisement, not in India, in the history of the world. Entire figure will cross 1 crore, if they are serious about what they are doing.
claims.relies_on: Projection from draft-stage removals plus BLO 'not recommended' rates (10.6% and 12.6% in two districts).
claims.check: A forecast. On the Commission's final roll it did not happen as projected: 3,66,742 more were removed after the draft and 21,53,343 added, so the final roll (7,41,92,357) was 47.7 lakh below the roll before.
claims.site_counts: Bihar final roll: net fall 47,72,808; the rise after the draft made up at most 27.2% of the draft removals (a ceiling, since it counts new voters).
claims.site_stops: 'Disenfranchisement' needs to know who was eligible; the lists record an officer's reason, not eligibility.

claims.quote: From 27 lakh after the January 2025 special summary revision, the number of adults who are not registered as voters has gone up to 81 lakh in the SIR.
claims.speaker_note: The Wire's paraphrase of his presentation.
claims.relies_on: Adult population projection against the final roll.
claims.check: Consistent with 8.22 crore adults (his October base) less the final roll of 7.42 crore.
claims.site_counts: Same method on the site's projection gives about 88 lakh adults off the final roll against 8.30 crore projected for March 2026.
claims.site_stops: As above: residents, not citizens or electors.

claims.quote: From the outset, I have said SIR is targeted at Bengal. As Bihar elections were only a few months away, the EC used the state as the testing ground to implement SIR. Now the BJP wants to go the whole hog in Bengal
claims.relies_on: None stated.
claims.check: An assertion of purpose made at a public meeting.
claims.site_counts: None.
claims.site_stops: The site makes no claim about purpose.

strongest_points: Measures the roll against the projected adult population rather than counting deletions alone, which catches unregistered young voters that a deletion count cannot see.
Pointed out early that women were removed more than men in Bihar, which the site's own count of the lists confirms in every district.
Raised data-quality findings on the final Bihar roll (5,17,216 entries with junk values, apparent duplicates) that are checkable against the roll.
overreach: 'Largest disenfranchisement in the history of the world' and 'will cross 1 crore' are forecasts and rhetoric, not counts; the final roll fell by about 48 lakh.
Attributes purpose to the BJP and the EC without evidence beyond the pattern of states chosen.
not_verified: His 2.5 crore figure for Bihar electors on the 2003 roll (against the ECI's 4.6 crore).
The 5,17,216 junk entries, 5,24,210 within-AC duplicates and 63,09,777 cross-AC duplicates (reported by The Wire, not recomputed).
His May 2026 interview with The Wire ('SIR Created a Model of Voter List Curation') is a video whose content could not be read; not used.
No 2025-26 column of his in The Indian Express or ThePrint on the SIR was found.

pieces.how_read: PDF, 80 pages, at reports/indian-express-plus-election-commission-2026-10.pdf in the site repository.

claims.quote: Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months – four times on a single day – to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge.
claims.relies_on: The Commissioners' notes on file, which the paper says it has seen ('The Indian Express has seen each of these exchanges').
claims.check: Fact as reported from documents the paper holds and the site has not seen. The Commission's reply acknowledged 'written notes' and 'differing views' without disputing that they exist.
claims.site_counts: Process page, 'Inside the Commission': each dated event with the special issue's page number; the count of 14 stays in prose.
claims.site_stops: The site has not seen the notes.

claims.quote: On May 16, Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded on file that the form 'cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960' ... Sandhu concurred on May 19. In July, the SIR declaration appeared on the online form anyway.
claims.relies_on: File notes; the online Form 6.
claims.check: The Form 6 declaration itself is publicly visible and was reported by the paper on 12 July 2026; the file notes are the paper's.
claims.site_counts: Process page, Form 6 section.
claims.site_stops: No count of applications affected.

claims.quote: Of the 294 seats that went to polls, in 49, the SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin. But in these, the spoils were almost evenly shared — 26 were won by BJP and 21 by TMC.
claims.relies_on: Adjudication deletions by constituency (same measure as Newslaundry's Test 3) against 2026 margins.
claims.check: Matches Newslaundry's Test 3 (49 seats; BJP 26, TMC 21, Congress 2). The paper's own words: 'There was no evidence of its role in the election outcome.'
claims.site_counts: West Bengal elections page measures the fall in the roll from 2024 instead (the CEO published no removals below the state): over the margin in 139 seats; AITC-won seats lost more per 100 (12.38) than BJP-won (9.41), and against their own district the gap is small (0.23 against 0.03).
claims.site_stops: Over the margin means large enough to decide a seat, not that it did.

claims.quote: the Supreme Court, in February 2026, [took] the last leg of the SIR out of the Commission's hands and get judicial officers to decide on the plight of 60 lakh voters flagged for 'logical discrepancies.' Of these, 27 lakh electors were subsequently deleted by the Commission.
claims.relies_on: Court orders; the Commission's figures; its affidavit (38 lakh appeals pending: 22.21 lakh by deleted voters, 16.10 lakh against inclusion).
claims.check: Matches the reported official totals.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal: 60,06,675 under adjudication; 27,16,393 not eligible; 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion, 49.3% of appeals.
claims.site_stops: Who filed the 16 lakh appeals against inclusion is not public; Sandhu's note asked the same question.

claims.quote: Goa's EROs heard these cases. On the documents produced, they found 97 voters eligible for the final roll. The software had no way to record that decision.
claims.relies_on: Eight emails and letters from the Goa CEO's office, 11 to 17 Feb 2026; the final roll of 21 Feb, which the paper checked name by name.
claims.check: Documentary, as reported.
claims.site_counts: Process page, Goa lane.
claims.site_stops: The site has not seen the emails.

entries.fact_vs_inference: The facts are the dated notes, letters and the Commission's replies. The inferences, labelled as analysis in 'What Election Commission rift reveals', are that centralising the roll software weakens the safeguard of decentralised EROs and that the Commission has not acted 'as far as possible, unanimously'. The paper does not claim the SIR changed the West Bengal result and says there was no evidence that it did.
strongest_points: Built on documents, dated, with the Commission given a questionnaire (no response) and its later press note reported in full.
Separates the process failures from the electoral outcome explicitly.
overreach: Little. 'Disquiet ... unprecedented in scale and significance' is the paper's judgement.
not_verified: The notes themselves; the site and this research have only the paper's account.

pieces.title: More SIR Deletions, Bigger BJP Swing? Prannoy Roy DeKodes the Data | DeKoder

claims.quote: In the 25 constituencies with the highest SIR deletion rates, the TMC had a swing against it of nearly 10.5% ... in the 25 constituency with the lowest SIR deletions, the swing against the TMC was down to only 5.3% ... [SIR] deletions almost doubled the swing against the TMC.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from word position in untimed auto-captions times the 7:37 runtime; +/- 15 seconds (see reads/video.md)
claims.relies_on: Unnamed; he lists ECI data and research by named outlets but no dataset for these figures.
claims.check: Not reproduced. A top-25 versus bottom-25 comparison with no controls; 'deletion rate' undefined.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal per 100 in the fall of the roll is highest in Kolkata North (27.98) and South (24.54), lowest in Purbo Medinipur (1.64): the top and bottom seats differ by region, not only by deletions. Bihar's seat-swing model shows how much this matters: without each seat's previous lead the slope is -0.83, with it +0.31, an interval that takes in no effect.
claims.site_stops: The vote cannot tell whether removals moved votes; the site has not run a West Bengal swing model.

claims.quote: women deletions accounted for 62% of all deleted names compared with only 38% of men voters deleted.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from word position in untimed auto-captions times the 7:37 runtime; +/- 15 seconds (see reads/video.md)
claims.relies_on: Unnamed; matches the Sabar Institute and BehanBox figure (61.8%), which covers names deleted or held under adjudication.
claims.check: Base differs from deletions alone.
claims.site_counts: Official counts give smaller shares: women 53.5% of the 58.2 lakh left off the draft (roll 49.2%), and 52.6% of the fall from the 2024 roll to the election roll; over-represented in 21 of 24 districts.
claims.site_stops: The CEO has published no split by sex of the adjudication outcomes.

claims.quote: In other words, the SIR deletion process clearly targeted Muslim voters ... Muslim voter deletions were at a 52% higher deletion rate than non-Muslims.
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from word position in untimed auto-captions times the 7:37 runtime; +/- 15 seconds (see reads/video.md)
claims.relies_on: Unstated; religion of deleted electors can only be guessed from names (as Sabar did, about 31 lakh).
claims.check: The rate comparison is internally consistent (30 / 19.8 lakh). 'Targeted' is a claim about purpose drawn from a correlation.
claims.site_counts: The site does not classify West Bengal's removals by religion. In Bihar, where it does from names, religion is a range, and the census share sits inside it in 18 of 38 districts and below the low bound in 20.
claims.site_stops: Names are a guess; the lists cannot show intent.

claims.quote: there's no doubt and there never has been any doubt that election [rolls] need to be constantly updated and cleaned up
claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from word position in untimed auto-captions times the 7:37 runtime; +/- 15 seconds (see reads/video.md)

strongest_points: Draft-stage removal rates he cites (Delhi about 33%, Maharashtra about 21%, Karnataka 20%) are right as reported.
Asks the Commission to explain imbalances by sex and religion, which is a request for data the site also lacks.
overreach: 'Almost doubled the swing' is causal from a raw comparison.
'Clearly targeted' asserts intent.
'These millions will now not be able to vote' ignores restoration through Form 6 and appeals.
not_verified: Source of the 10.5% and 5.3% swing figures; the 30 lakh Muslim deletions; the survey premises (13-point gender gap for TMC; 7-8% against 75% Muslim support); his own deletion; his dates for the Express piece (he says 21 Sep; it is 23 Sep) and Nariman's remarks (6 Oct).

claims.quote: A majority of respondents, 52%, do not have a birth certificate. Furthermore, 41% lack a domicile certificate and 42% do not possess a caste certificate.
claims.relies_on: 3,054 face-to-face interviews in Assam, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi.

claims.site_stops: Holding a document is not the same as being removed: in the SIR's later phases most electors were mapped to the 2002-05 roll and were not asked for documents, and Aadhaar was admitted after 14 Aug 2025 (Supreme Court).

claims.quote: three-quarters of the citizens who have none of the required documents belong to the lower half of the economic order.
claims.relies_on: Same survey.
claims.check: As reported.
claims.site_counts: Not measured.

claims.quote: the current requirements could pose a 'serious challenge for many of those who have a legitimate right to be part of the voters' list.'
claims.relies_on: Survey authors' conclusion.
claims.check: A risk statement, hedged.

pieces.title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority

claims.quote: If we restrict ourselves to the adjudicated SIR deletions, and even if we make the incredibly heroic assumption that every deleted voter would have obediently turned out, and that every such voter would have voted for the runner-up ... that flips a maximum of 26 ACs away from the BJP. The resulting number, 207-26 =181, leaves the BJP comfortably above the 148-seat majority threshold
claims.relies_on: ECI 2026 results; CEO West Bengal PN-05/2026 (28 Feb 2026); AC-wise adjudication tally; Sabar Institute's AC-level digitisation, which he checks against the press note within 0.1%.
claims.check: Bound computed under stated assumptions; agrees with Newslaundry and The Wire's Aparna Bhattacharya (25).
claims.site_counts: Same press note totals as the site (76,637,529 before; 5,820,899 left off the draft; 6,006,675 held; 2,716,393 not eligible).
claims.site_stops: The site has no adjudication outcome by constituency from the CEO, so it does not run this bound.

claims.quote: Under any neutral calibration, the BJP retains majority by more than thirty seats. The deletions hypothesis only reverses this result at extreme calibrations that the data refuse to support
claims.relies_on: A two-parameter counterfactual (turnout and partisanship of restored voters) anchored by a cross-seat regression.
claims.check: His full-heroism 'contestable' bound (adjudicated plus shifted and absent) flips 69 seats and leaves the BJP ten short; he argues that assumption is implausible (at 92% turnout, 95% would need to vote against the BJP).
claims.site_counts: Bihar's impact estimate uses the same logic: in 187 of 243 seats the runner-up could not have won with every removed voter; 4 to 6 seats change hands both ways.
claims.site_stops: No one knows how removed electors would have voted; the site carries a break-even figure where it cannot assume one.

claims.quote: BJP MLAs were associated with more adjudicated deletions in their own seats, about 15 more per thousand voters ... It is consistent with the strategic-targeting story for the adjudication channel ... But the offsetting movement in non-adjudicated deletions along the same dimensions means that the overall contestable rate ... shows no partisan-targeting signal.
claims.relies_on: OLS across 294 seats, HC1 errors; he says it is a correlation exercise, not causal identification.
claims.check: His strongest evidence for targeting, stated with its limit.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal per 100 by 2026 winner, against the district: BJP-won 0.03, AITC-won 0.23 above their districts (the fall in the roll, not adjudication).
claims.site_stops: Different measure; the site has no adjudication by seat.

claims.quote: This is not an argument that the SIR did not matter. It clearly mattered in particular constituencies ... Why individuals had to be put through this ordeal in this particular election, with many plausibly denied their constitutional rights, is a question that should hold our attention.

strongest_points: States every assumption and shows how the answer moves with it; separates the adjudication channel (where a partisan pattern appears) from the BLO channel (where it does not).
overreach: Treats the 24.2 lakh entered as dead as 'defensible' removals and drops them; the site's Bihar test found deaths entered at about 3.4 years' worth, with women over-represented, so 'dead' is itself an officer's entry.
not_verified: His Table 4 estimates were not recomputed.

claims.quote: If we compare the 2026 winning margins to the net deletions in each constituency, we get 82 BJP-won constituencies where deletions exceeded the party's victory margin. Of these, 70 were seats that flipped from TMC to BJP.

claims.site_stops: Over the margin is a size test, not an effect.

claims.quote: An even stricter test, comparing UA deletions to the electoral swing from 2021, shows that in 14 seats, the deletions were higher than the overall change in margin. Of these 14, the BJP won only one – Pandabeswar – and the TMC won the rest in 2026.
claims.relies_on: Same.
claims.check: As published.
claims.site_counts: Not run on the site.

Whether that overlap reflects correction, disenfranchisement, or some combination of both may remain unresolved. That is a question of public interest that warrants a full and transparent answer, something which the Election Commission refuses to provide.

strongest_points: Four tests of increasing strictness, each stated, with the answer shrinking from 82 seats to one; explicitly declines a causal claim.

Estimating how the removed would have voted moves 4 to 6 seats, in both directions, and the NDA keeps a majority on every estimate (data/bihar/impact.json, summary.booth_lower.flips 4, booth_upper.flips 6). claims.timestamp_note: approximate: estimated from the quote's position in YouTube's untimed English auto-caption text (via a Firecrawl scrape) times the 54:52 runtime; the livestream opens before he speaks and long Hindi passages are garbled in the captions, so treat as +/- 5 minutes

claims.quote: It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP. He and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable
claims.relies_on: The Commission's press note 120 of 26 September 2026 and the Supreme Court's remark of 5 October 2026 that it had not approved any modified Form 6.
claims.check: Two parts hold on the record the site keeps; one does not. The Form 6 declaration was added without amending the Rules over two Commissioners' written objections (as the Express reported), and the Supreme Court said on 5 October that it had not approved any modified Form 6. On 12 October it said it had neither approved nor disapproved the new form, which did not exist when the Bihar case was heard (Bar and Bench and the Hindustan Times, 12 Oct 2026). Whether it was illegal has not been decided by any court. That it was done 'to help the BJP' is his inference.
claims.site_counts: Disputes page: court-31 (LiveLaw, 5 Oct 2026, 'Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us'); process-03 (Express, 12 Jul 2026, the change reported); process-04 (the Commissioners' objections); process-05 (Express, 30 Sep 2026, the declaration removed from the online form in states whose final roll is out). All in data/india/disputes.json. The Commission's reply is soft-28.
claims.site_stops: The site cannot say who made the change; the Commission has not said, and says all its decisions were unanimous.

claims.quote: reportedly reflected a reduction of approximately 20.66 lakh names from the electorate of about 2.14 crore recorded in June 2026

claims.site_counts: Punjab: roll before 2,14,61,043, names left off the draft 20,66,635, or 9.6 per 100 (data/india/states.json, Punjab row, electors_before, removed, per_100). Final roll of 12 Oct 2026: 2,01,00,727, with 7,97,263 added and 86,038 removed after the draft, so a net fall of 13,60,343, 6.3 per 100 (electors_final, added_after_draft, removed_after_draft, net_fall, net_fall_per_100). Of those left off, 5,74,568 were entered as dead, 13,56,846 as shifted, absent or other, 1,19,145 as duplicate.

claims.quote: The names deleted from the electoral rolls include those who have died, those who are not Indian citizens, those who are registered in multiple places and those who have shifted permanently. The responsibility to create the electoral roll is of the ERO [electoral registration officer]. So every ERO and every district magistrate has this data

claims.check: No published count shows anyone removed in Bihar as a non-citizen. None of the reasons in the published removal records is citizenship. The Supreme Court later directed the Commission to refer any cases it deleted as non-citizens to the competent authority, which shows such cases may exist, but no number has been published.
claims.site_counts: Phase 1 lists: four reasons, dead, shifted, absent, already enrolled, totalling 65,59,626 (data/bihar/reasons.json, totals). After the draft, Format 4B lists 3,66,742 removed: 62,441 expired, 2,12,999 shifted, 81,334 repeated, 9,968 with no reason stated (data/bihar/final.json, totals.r_expired, r_shifted, r_repeated, r_unstated). claims.site_stops: The site says nothing about whether any person is a citizen. The reason a name was removed is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

claims.quote: Many times, if any individual who is not an Indian citizen and who has got some papers made, you would have noticed, that in the enumeration phase we will match whether in 2002, 2003 or 2004, either you or your senior relatives were on the electoral rolls or not. If there is a match, then the matter ends there. Those who do not match, they will be issued a notice, after this they will have to show their papers and say where they were in 2003. Doing this is very necessary
claims.translation: The Wire's English; the original was likely Hindi and was not seen.
claims.relies_on: Press conference of 27 Oct 2025 announcing phase 2.
claims.check: Describes the phase 2 procedure as the site records it. The notices that followed are counted in crores; a notice records that the elector could not be linked to the old roll or that the entry showed a discrepancy, not a finding about citizenship.

Across the 21 states with a published total, 13,06,52,476 electors on the drafts were sent a notice, 21.1 per 100 (data/india/notices.json, notices_total, per_100).

claims.quote: The most compelling testament to the success of the SIR in Bihar was that not a single appeal was filed against the final electoral roll, establishing its sanctity and credibility
claims.relies_on: The Commission's own count of appeals, not published.
claims.check: The site has no count of appeals in Bihar, so it cannot confirm or refute zero. It does show that a missing appeal is a weak test: the Supreme Court in May 2026 opened judicial review to people wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate, and Amit Shah said on 29 Oct 2025 that three appeals had been filed after the SIR.
claims.site_counts: Bihar, from the Commission's return: 65,59,409 left off the draft; 21,53,343 added and 3,66,742 removed after it; final roll 7,41,92,357, a net fall of 47,72,808 from the roll before (data/bihar/final.json, totals.p1, added, removed_after, final, net_fall). claims.quote: All decisions of the Election Commission of India, including SIR [the ongoing special intensive revision of electoral rolls], have been unanimous and with the approval of both the Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner
claims.relies_on: The Commission's source-based clarification of 23 Sep 2026, followed by a written press note saying 'Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution.'

The Express reports that at least one, Sandhu's of 13 August 2026, called the Form 6 change 'unauthorised/illegal' and directed its removal, which sits uneasily with the change having been approved by both Commissioners. The Commission later removed the declaration from the online form.

claims.quote: The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English, not his words verbatim.

claims.check: The first part matches the records: deaths and duplicates are recorded reasons in every state. The last part has no count behind it anywhere the site has looked, and the largest group of removals in the records is neither dead nor duplicate.
claims.site_counts: Across 31 states, 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts: 2,79,69,558 dead (20.9%), 9,56,35,923 shifted, absent or other (71.5%), 1,01,48,459 duplicate (7.6%) (data/india/states.json, total.removed, dead, shifted_absent_other, duplicate, shares).

claims.quote: He said that even if the opposition boycotts the House 200 times, we will not allow even a single illegal infiltrator to vote in the country. The Home Minister said that the government’s policy is to Detect, Delete, and Deport, and we will carry out this work through constitutional processes.
claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English.
claims.relies_on: Government policy statement.
claims.check: A statement of intent, not a count. The Supreme Court held in May 2026 that the Commission's enquiry is into eligibility for enrolment, that declining to enrol someone does not declare them not to be a citizen, and that deciding citizenship belongs to the authority under the Citizenship Act.
claims.site_counts: data/india/nrc.json, sir_vs_nrc-10 and sir_vs_nrc-12 (2026 INSC 564, paras 176 and 186). data/india/disputes.json, soft-16: the Commission's instructions of 14 May 2026 tell registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to the competent authority.
claims.site_stops: The site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen.

claims.quote: Union Home Minister said that the beginning of our democratic history was in 1952, and the first Special Intensive Revision took place in 1952. ... He said that after 2004, the next Special Intensive Revision is taking place only in 2025, and no political party has ever opposed this process till date
claims.translation: PIB's reported speech in English.
claims.check: The site does not hold the earlier revisions and cannot check that list. It does show that the 2002-04 revision is the base every state is mapped to now, which agrees with his last date. 'No political party has ever opposed this process' is contradicted for the current revision by the record of court petitions and Assembly resolutions.
claims.site_counts: Mapping years by state: 2002 (West Bengal, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Goa), 2003 (Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Bihar), 2005 and 2006 elsewhere (data/india/process.json, timeline). Disputes page: 42 court items, 2 Assembly resolutions and 34 protests (data/india/disputes.json, sections courts, resolutions, protests).
claims.site_stops: The site has not researched revisions before 2002.

claims.quote: Till now, the EC has only removed the names of the infiltrators from the electoral rolls, but we will remove them from the soil of Bengal.
claims.translation: The Indian Express's English. The Telegraph renders the same sentence as 'While the Election Commission (EC) has only removed infiltrators from the electoral rolls of West Bengal, the larger task would be to drive them out of the country's borders.'
claims.relies_on: West Bengal's SIR removals (the Express says he was referring to 'over 89 lakh' names; The Telegraph says 'nearly 91 lakh').
claims.check: The West Bengal records do not support reading the removals as infiltrators. The largest single reason entered at the draft is death; the adjudication found 27,16,393 not eligible without a published reason, and more than 22 lakh of them and others appealed.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal: 58,20,899 left off the draft, 24,16,852 entered as dead, 32,65,719 shifted, absent or other, 1,38,328 duplicate (data/india/states.json, West Bengal row). Under adjudication 60,06,675: 32,68,119 found eligible, 27,16,393 not eligible; 22,21,118 appeals by the excluded and 16,10,311 against inclusion, 37,05,235 pending (data/westbengal/summary.json, adj).
claims.site_stops: No published figure counts removals by citizenship. 'Not eligible' in adjudication is not a finding that a person is a foreigner, and the site says nothing about whether anyone is a citizen.

not_verified: His Hindi words in the Lok Sabha and at Cooch Behar; PIB and the Express give English.
The count of three appeals in Bihar.
The list of revisions from 1952 to 2004.

claims.quote: कहा कि 18 वर्ष से ज्यादा उम्र के हर शख्स का नाम मतदाता सूची में होना चाहिए और इस तरह उत्तर प्रदेश में मतदाताओं की संख्या 16 करोड़ होनी चाहिए। सीएम योगी ने कहा कि हालांकि एसआईआर के बाद मतदाता सूची में जो नाम आए हैं, वे 12 करोड़ हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि यह चार करोड़ का अंतर है। जनवरी 2025 की मतदाता सूची में कुल 15 करोड़ 44 लाख नाम थे।
claims.translation: Every voter over 18 should be on the roll, so this number should be 16 crore. And how many names have come onto the roll after the SIR? 12 crore. This gap of 4 crore. The roll of January 2025 had 15 crore 44 lakh names.
claims.relies_on: His own arithmetic: a population of about 25 crore times 65 per cent adults, set against the count of enumeration forms collected by mid-December 2025.
claims.check: Two of his three numbers hold. The roll before the revision was 15,44,30,092 (data/uttarpradesh/summary.json, roll_before), which is his 15 crore 44 lakh. The draft of 6 January 2026 held 12,55,56,025 (summary.json, draft), close to his 12 crore. His 16 crore of eligible adults is near the site's projection of 16,16,85,000 people aged 18 and over on 1 March 2026 (analysis.json, rolls.adults_2026). The 'gap of four crore' mixes two comparisons. Against the old roll the draft was 2,88,74,067 smaller (summary.json, left_off), 2.89 crore. Against projected adults it was 3.61 crore smaller. The roll before held 95.5 per 100 projected adults, the draft 77.7 and the final roll 82.9 (analysis.json, rolls.before_per_100_adults, draft_per_100_adults, final_per_100_adults).
claims.site_counts: Roll before 15,44,30,092; draft 12,55,56,025; names left off 2,88,74,067, 18.7 per 100; final roll 13,39,84,792 on 10 April 2026, a net rise of 84,28,767 from the draft (summary.json: roll_before, draft, left_off, per_100, final, net_rise). Projected adults 16,16,85,000 (analysis.json, rolls.adults_2026).
claims.site_stops: The projection counts residents, so it includes people registered in another state; 'should be 16 crore' is an upper bound on who could be on Uttar Pradesh's roll.

claims.quote: उन्होंने कार्यकर्ताओं से कहा कि यह जो चार करोड़ का अंतर है। वह आपका विरोधी नहीं है, इसमें से 85 से 90 प्रतिशत आपका मतदाता है।
claims.translation: This gap of 4 crore is missing. It is not your opponent. 85 to 90 per cent of it is your voter.
claims.relies_on: No source given. The Hindustan Times quotes the same line in English: 'This is not your opponent's voters. Eighty-five to 90 per cent of these missing voters are ours.' The Indian Express has '90 per cent'.
claims.check: Nothing published records how any removed elector votes, so the share cannot be checked. What the site can set beside it is where the removals fell. They were heaviest in the cities: 28.1 per 100 on the urban roll against 15.3 on the rural one (analysis.json, urban.urban_per_100, rural_per_100, the Chief Electoral Officer's figures as the Hindustan Times printed them), and Lucknow lost the most names, 30.0 per 100 (summary.json, top). Spread over constituencies by district, seats the NDA won in 2022 lost about 19.1 per 100 and seats the SP alliance won about 17.7 (analysis.json, margins.alliances). That is a small difference in the places, and says nothing about the people removed.
claims.site_counts: Urban 28.12 and rural 15.25 per 100 left off (analysis.json, urban); NDA-held seats 19.14 and SP-alliance seats 17.69 per 100, district rates spread over seats (analysis.json, margins.alliances).
claims.site_stops: The site cannot say whom any removed elector would have voted for.

claims.quote: सीएम योगी ने दावा किया कि हाल में जब वह एक जनपद के दौरे पर गए थे, जहां मतदाता सूची में विरोधियों द्वारा भरे गए एसआईआर फॉर्मों में कुछ बांग्लादेशी नागरिकों के नाम भी पाए गए। उन्होंने दावा किया, एक जगह तो यह भी मैंने देखा एक सज्जन का नाम था, उसकी उम्र 20 साल है, उसके पिता की उम्र 30 साल और उसके दादा की उम्र 40 साल थी
claims.translation: Look, I just went to a district. In the SIR forms filled in the roll there, many by opponents, there are names of some Bangladeshis too. Tell me, in one place I even saw a gentleman's name, his age 20, his father's age 30 and his grandfather's age 40.
claims.relies_on: His own visit to an unnamed district. No figure given.
claims.check: No published figure counts removals by citizenship. The draft roll's reasons, as officers entered them, are dead, untraceable or absent, permanently shifted, enrolled more than once and others (summary.json, reasons). After the draft, 8,15,996 more names came off; the press reported 2,069 of them recorded as under age or not citizens (data/uttarpradesh/raw/sir_state_summary.csv, removed_after_draft_underage_or_noncitizen, from The New Indian Express of 11 April 2026). That is an officer's entry and nobody checked it. Age gaps between generations are the kind of mismatch the Commission's 'logical discrepancy' check flags; the press reported 2.22 crore such notices in Uttar Pradesh (data/india/notices.json, discrepancy, press).
claims.site_counts: Reasons at the draft: dead 46,23,796; untraceable or absent 79,52,190; shifted 1,29,77,472; multiple 25,47,207; others 7,73,402 (summary.json, reasons). Removed after the draft 8,15,996, of which 2,069 under age or not citizens, press (analysis.json, notices.removed_after).
claims.site_stops: The site says nothing about whether any person or group are citizens.

claims.quote: Identifying ineligible names illegally included in the voter list and removing them as per rules is essential for India's security, unity and integrity
claims.relies_on: His post on X, as rendered by PTI. PTI adds that he 'said verification of entries relating to deceased persons, those who had permanently shifted and duplicate entries was necessary'.
claims.check: The reasons officers wrote down at the draft are almost all about people who died, moved or are listed twice, and none is about illegal inclusion. Dead were 16.0 per cent of the names left off, untraceable or absent 27.5, shifted 44.9, enrolled more than once 8.8 and others 2.7 (summary.json, shares). The one reason near his word 'illegally', under age or not a citizen, covered 2,069 names after the draft, as reported. Most of those who came off after the draft were people sent a notice who did not answer: 3,50,026 of 8,15,996, press (analysis.json, notices.removed_after.no_response).
claims.site_counts: Shares of names left off by reason (summary.json, shares). Notices 3.26 crore, press (analysis.json, notices.all); removed after the draft 8,15,996, press.
claims.site_stops: A reason is what an officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. The site does not say whether anyone on or off the roll is a citizen.
claims.translation: Every aware voter should keep in mind that identifying ineligible names illegally entered in the voter list and removing them according to the rules is essential for India's security, unity and integrity.

claims.quote: আমার প্রথম প্রশ্ন, অসমে কেন করলেন না SIR? আসলে অসমে ভুয়ো ভোটে জেতেন। এসআইআর করলে অসমে হেরে যেতেন। আমার দ্বিতীয় প্রশ্ন, উত্তর পূর্ব ভারতের রাজ্যগুলোতে কেন এসআইআর করলেন না? ত্রিপুরা দিয়েও তো বাংলাদেশিরা ঢোকে।
claims.translation: My first question: why did you not do the SIR in Assam? In fact you win Assam on fake votes. If you did the SIR you would lose Assam. My second question: why did you not do the SIR in the states of the North-East? Bangladeshis come in through Tripura too.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's order of 27 October 2025, which named twelve states and union territories for the second phase and left out Assam and the North-East.
claims.check: The fact about the process held when she said it. Assam was given a 'Special Revision' with no forms and no link to an earlier roll, by the Commission's letter of 17 November 2025, and never had an SIR (data/india/process.json, timeline 'Assam gets a different revision'; data/assam/summary.json). The North-East was added later: the order of 14 May 2026 put Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Tripura in the third phase (process.json, schedules). Tripura's enumeration ran 15 September to 14 October 2026 and its draft is due on 21 October. Her claims about fake votes in Assam and about who crosses through Tripura are not things the site's records can test.
claims.site_counts: Phase of each state (process.json, schedules). Assam: 10,56,291 names flagged as dead, shifted or multiple, never shown as removed from the draft (data/assam/summary.json, state.flagged).
claims.site_stops: The site does not say whether any person or group are citizens, and nothing it holds counts entries by nationality.

claims.quote: Several others have lost their lives since this process began… a revision that earlier took three years is now being forced into three months.
claims.relies_on: Her letter to the Chief Election Commissioner. The Telegraph's ellipsis is kept.
claims.check: The three months is about right for the schedule as first ordered. House-to-house enumeration in West Bengal ran from 4 November to 4 December 2025, later to 11 December, the draft came on 16 December, and the final roll was due on 7 February, then 14 February, and was published on 28 February 2026 (process.json, schedules, West Bengal). That is about four months from the first house visit to the final roll, and the 60,06,675 names put under adjudication were decided after it (data/westbengal/summary.json, pn05.adjudication). The site holds no record of how long earlier intensive revisions took, so 'three years' is not checked here.
claims.site_counts: West Bengal schedule (process.json). Two West Bengal deaths in the site's list of deaths reported during the revision, both reported after this letter (data/india/disputes.json, section deaths).
claims.site_stops: The site does not count deaths.

claims.quote: More than 110 people have already died; every day, three to four people are dying out of SIR anxiety
claims.relies_on: No list given in the report. The figure rose over the weeks: The Hindu and NDTV reported her giving 39 deaths in December 2025, when the state announced compensation (search excerpts; those pages were not opened).
claims.check: No official count of deaths linked to the revision has been published, so neither 110 nor three to four a day can be checked. The site's list of deaths reported during the revision has eight items across India, two of them in West Bengal: a 75-year-old man who died after falling ill in a hearing queue in Birbhum, and an 82-year-old man in Purulia whose son filed an FIR after he died, allegedly by suicide, hours before a hearing (data/india/disputes.json, section deaths, 11 and 21 January 2026). Each is a press report of what a family alleged.
claims.site_counts: Eight reported deaths in the list, two in West Bengal (disputes.json, deaths). The site does not keep a running count.
claims.site_stops: The site cannot say how many people died, or why.

claims.quote: SIR was conducted in Bengal to capture the state. Ninety-three lakh names were either deleted or put under adjudication.
claims.relies_on: No source given in the report.
claims.check: The 93 lakh is near the site's figures, depending on what is added up. The draft left off 58,20,899; 5,46,053 more came off on Form 7 after the draft; 60,06,675 were put under adjudication, and of those 27,16,393 were found not eligible, as reported (data/westbengal/summary.json, pn05.removed, pn05.form7, adj.under_adjudication, adj.found_not_eligible). Draft, Form 7 and not eligible add to 90,83,345, about 91 lakh. Adding all those put under adjudication, most of whom were kept, gives 1.24 crore. Below the state the site has only the fall in the roll: from the 2024 roll to the roll the 2026 election was held on, 77,58,998 (summary.json, fall). That fall was larger than the winning margin in 139 of 294 seats, and larger than the margin at the seat's turnout in 132 (summary.json, over_margin, could_change). Larger than the margin means the removals could have decided a seat, never that they did. Nothing in the records shows why the revision was run.
claims.site_counts: Removed at the draft 58,20,899; Form 7 after the draft 5,46,053; under adjudication 60,06,675, of which 32,68,119 found eligible and 27,16,393 not eligible, as reported (summary.json, pn05 and adj; data/westbengal/raw/adjudication_state.csv). Fall in the roll 2024 to election 77,58,998; over the margin in 139 seats (summary.json).
claims.site_stops: The site cannot show intent. The adjudication outcomes are state totals as reported, and below the state there is only the fall in the roll.

claims.relies_on: The Collective's scrape of every Form 7 the UP Chief Electoral Officer's website displayed, with a team of data analysts. The scraped file is not published.
claims.check: The arithmetic holds (85,854 / 87,127 = 98.5%). The same report says the 87,127 were all filed between 15 March and 2 April 2026, more than 4.3 lakh Form 7s were filed in all, and 62 forms carried a single letter as the reason and 1,211 'absent/shifted'. The CEO's office called the claim misleading but no outlet read reports him disputing the number (see the claims from rc-oct14 and ceo-x).
claims.site_counts: Uttar Pradesh's draft of 6 January 2026 left off 2,88,74,067 of 15,44,30,092 names (18.7 per 100). The final roll of 10 April 2026 was 13,39,84,792, a net rise of 84,28,767 from the draft of 12,55,56,025. 8,15,996 names were deleted after the draft, as the press reported the CEO, of which 3,50,026 did not answer a notice (data/uttarpradesh/summary.json, roll_before, left_off, final, net_rise, removed_after; data/uttarpradesh/analysis.json, notices.removed_after). The site holds 2,68,682 Form 7s filed from 6 January to 6 March 2026, as The Hindu reported the CEO (data/uttarpradesh/raw/sir_state_summary.csv; summary.json form7).
claims.site_stops: The site has no count of Form 7s after 6 March and no count of officers' Form 7s, so it cannot check the 85,854 or the 4.3 lakh. How many of the 8,15,996 deletions came through these forms is not published.

claims.quote: But the officers did not fill the forms. The ECI’s own software, ERONET automatically generated these forms, when officials deleted voters during the SIR hearings. The auto-generated forms came loaded with the officers’ digital signatures and were sent up for approval by their seniors.
claims.relies_on: Interviews with four assembly-level election officials (unnamed) and the pattern in the scraped data.
claims.check: Rests on four unnamed officials, not on a document the Collective publishes. The CEO's office did not deny that the software produced the forms: it said notices, hearings and recorded orders came first (claim from ceo-x). Bharat Samachar (10 Oct 2026) reports the office as saying the forms were generated by the software to keep a record of electors found ineligible; that report gives no direct quotation and was not used as a claim.
claims.site_counts: Notices went to 3.26 crore of the 12.56 crore on the draft, 1.04 crore with no mapping and 2.22 crore for logical discrepancies, as the CEO told The Times of India (data/uttarpradesh/analysis.json, notices.all, no_mapping, discrepancy; data/india/notices.json, Uttar Pradesh). 3,50,026 were deleted for not answering a notice (analysis.json, notices.removed_after.no_response).
claims.site_stops: The site has no record of how ERONET works or who signed which form.

claims.quote: In our investigation, we also found that a total of 1,10,476 voter deletion requests were submitted by individuals and accepted by the ECI after the legally mandated deadline.
claims.relies_on: The same scrape, read against the claims and objections deadline.
claims.check: Which date the Collective takes as the deadline is not stated in the sentence. The report treats the window between the draft (6 January) and the final roll (10 April) as the claims period in one place and says all the officers' forms came after the deadline in another, so the second reader should confirm the date it used.
claims.site_counts: The site's schedule for Uttar Pradesh is in data/uttarpradesh/analysis.json (schedule) and data/india/process.json. The Form 7 count it holds runs only to 6 March 2026 (2,68,682).
claims.site_stops: The site cannot say which Form 7s were filed late or what became of them.

claims.quote: In Tarabganj and Pilibhit assembly constituencies, 90 percent of the deletion requests filed were against Muslims.
claims.relies_on: The scraped Form 7s for two constituencies. The report does not say how it decided who was Muslim; presumably from names.
claims.check: Method not stated. The surrounding text names a person in whose name objections were filed; that sentence is left out here because it names a private person. Flagged for the owner: the site does not rest findings on religion guessed from names outside Bihar, and the case-study rules leave out items that rest on religion.
claims.site_counts: The site's seat figures for Uttar Pradesh are estimates spread from district totals by 2022 electors (data/uttarpradesh/seats.csv), with no Form 7 count and no religion.
claims.site_stops: The site has nothing by religion for Uttar Pradesh and cannot check this.

claims.quote: Yet, in his video, Rinwa confirmed our finding that the ECI software had forced election officers in UP to sign 85,854 forms to delete voters without stating a reason.
claims.speaker_note: The Collective's reading of the CEO's video; the video was not opened.
claims.relies_on: The CEO's recorded video of 9 October 2026, as the Collective watched it.
claims.check: The Collective quotes no sentence of the video in which he confirms the count, so 'confirmed' is its inference from his not disputing it. The CEO's office called the claim misleading in its statement (claim from ceo-x).

claims.quote: “The total number of names against which [bulk] deletion complaints were made through these Form 7s was only about 4,700. In Uttar Pradesh, which has a population in crores and where we have 13.39 crore [voters]. They found only 4,700 such names where there were multiple Form 7s,” said Rinwa.
claims.speaker_note: Navdeep Rinwa, in his recorded video, as the Collective quotes him (brackets the Collective's). The language of the original and whether this is a translation are not stated.
claims.relies_on: His own count of names that drew several Form 7s, with no source given.
claims.check: His 13.39 crore matches the final roll. The 4,700 answers a different finding of the Collective (the bulk objections in two constituencies), not the 85,854 officers' forms. It sits close to the 4,336 deletions from third-party Form 7s he gave in February (claim from ceo-feb).
claims.site_counts: Final roll 13,39,84,792 on 10 April 2026 (data/uttarpradesh/summary.json, final; data/india/raw/final.csv, Uttar Pradesh).
claims.site_stops: The site has no count of names that drew more than one Form 7.

claims.quote: यूपी एसआईआर में 85,854 फार्म-7 स्वतः बनाकर बिना कारण मतदाताओं के नाम हटाने का दावा भ्रामक है। संबंधित मामलों में नोटिस, सुनवाई, जांच और आदेश के बाद कार्रवाई हुई। 6 मार्च के बाद लंबित मामलों पर निर्णय भी नियमानुसार हुए। सही जानकारी के लिए आधिकारिक स्रोतों पर भरोसा करें।
claims.translation: "Claims that 85,854 Form-7 entries were auto-generated to delete UP voters without reason during SIR are misleading. Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure." (IANS's English, The Hans India, 13 Oct 2026, which omits the last sentence, 'Rely on official sources for correct information'.)
claims.speaker_note: The Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's office, on X, as IANS printed it.
claims.relies_on: The office's account of its procedure. No figures.
claims.check: It denies the description, not the number: it does not say how many forms there were or why they carried no reason. 'Pending cases were decided after 6 March' agrees with the Collective's dates (15 March to 2 April) for the officers' forms. The original post was not opened.
claims.site_counts: 8,15,996 deleted after the draft as the press reported the CEO: 3,50,026 for not answering a notice, 3,28,960 shifted, 79,076 multiple entries, 55,865 dead and 2,069 under age or not citizens (data/uttarpradesh/analysis.json, notices.removed_after).
claims.site_stops: The CEO has not published how many of those deletions went through a Form 7 and how many through a notice, and the site cannot say.

claims.quote: “Against a total of 12.55 crore voters during the claims and objections period (Jan 6–Feb 16), only 23,935 names have been deleted so far,” he said.
claims.speaker_note: Navdeep Rinwa, as The Times of India quotes him.
claims.relies_on: The CEO's own running count to 16 February 2026.
claims.check: An interim figure, eight weeks before the final roll. The same report splits the 23,935 into 14,388 after Form 8 transfers, 5,211 after an elector's own transfer request and 4,336 from third-party Form 7s, and gives 1.35 lakh Form 7s from 6 January to 16 February.
claims.site_counts: Draft 12,55,56,025 (data/uttarpradesh/summary.json, draft). By the final roll, 8,15,996 had been deleted after the draft (summary.json, removed_after, press).
claims.site_stops: The site has the end figure only as the press reported it, and nothing between February and April.

claims.quote: During the special period designated for filing claims and objections – typically known as the Summary Revision period – an individual voter is allowed to submit a maximum of 10 Form 7 applications.
claims.speaker_note: PTI's account of the Commission's letter, not the letter's words.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's letter of 9 October 2026 to Chief Electoral Officers, as PTI reported it.
claims.check: PTI and News On AIR both give 10 for the claims period and five a month in continuous updation. The Collective's follow-up says the order allowed no more than 30 objections a month (rc-oct14), which matches neither. The Collective also says the Commission had earlier removed a cap on bulk applications from the SIR protocol; that was not checked. PTI ties the order to bulk filing reported from Karnataka and Odisha, not to Uttar Pradesh.
claims.site_stops: The site holds no Form 7 counts per objector.
claims.site_files: data/india/process.json (if the order is added to the timeline)

strongest_points: A count from the Chief Electoral Officer's own published Form 7s, with a stated denominator (85,854 of 87,127) and dates, which anyone with the same pages could repeat.
The CEO's office answered the description and not the number, and no outlet read reports it disputing the count.
overreach: 'Rinwa confirmed our finding' rests on what he did not say in the video; the Collective quotes no sentence in which he confirms it.
The '30 objections in a month' does not match the Commission's order as PTI and News On AIR report it (10 in the claims period, five a month afterwards).
not_verified: The CEO's X post and recorded video were not opened; the X text is as IANS printed it, and the video only as the Collective quotes it.

OpIndia's report of the CEO's response (https://www.opindia.com/2026/10/up-ceo-rejects-reporters-collectives-allegations-of-mass-voter-deletions-says-85854-form-7-entries-were-generated-after-due-process/) would not open (403, Cloudflare).
The Commission's letter of 9 October 2026 itself; the cap is as PTI and News On AIR report it.
The scraped Form 7 file behind the 85,854, 87,127, 1,10,476 and 4.3 lakh, which the Collective has not published.
No Hindustan Times or Dainik Bhaskar report quoting the CEO on this was found in the time available.

claims.quote: The Election Commission has also ordered a special drive to identify and enrol eligible voters who may have been left out during SIR.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's letter on a special drive after the SIR.
claims.check: The Commission's letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II) of 1 October 2026 orders such a drive (on the reading list, round4.json). Its outcome is not yet published.

claims.quote: The Election Commission’s published material states that SIR is intended to ensure that eligible voters are included while ineligible entries are removed, with mechanisms for claims, objections and appeals. In Bihar’s 2025 SIR, the final roll included about 7.42 crore electors, after additions and deletions during the revision process.
claims.speaker_note: The video's description. A stray object-replacement character (U+FFFC) follows 'process.' in the description and is left out.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's stated purpose, and Bihar's final roll.
claims.check: Bihar's final roll was 7,41,92,357, which rounds to 7.42 crore. The sentence gives the end figure and not the change: the roll before the revision was about 7.89 crore.
claims.site_counts: Bihar's roll fell from about 7.89 crore before the revision (7,89,69,844 in the Commission's June 2025 total) to 7,24,05,756 on the draft and 7,41,92,357 on the final roll of 30 September 2025, a net fall of 47,73,025. 65,59,626 names were left off the draft and 3,66,742 deleted after it (data/india/states.json, Bihar electors_final, net_fall, removed, removed_after_draft; data/bihar/final.json).
claims.site_stops: The site counts names, not who was eligible.

claims.quote: From the alleged removal of 13 crore voters to questions around Form 6, ECINET, Gen Z voters, the role of Election Commissioners, Vote Chori and AI — this video examines eight major questions surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and the electoral-roll process.

pieces.how_read: Fetched with curl on 15 October 2026; body read from the page's JSON-LD. An earlier press conference in Delhi. In reported speech, Business Today says 'He compared the figure with the 2024 Lok Sabha election, saying the NDA-opposition gap was about 2% and the deleted names amounted to roughly 13-14% of the electorate.' That is the paper's paraphrase, not his words, and it is the only source found that says what the 2 per cent is a gap between.

claims.quote: The margin of victory in 2024 was just 2 per cent. Over 13 crore voters deleted — around 14 percent.
claims.speaker_note: PTI's evening copy. PTI's afternoon copy (dk-pti-am), ETV Bharat and National Herald give the same sentence ending at 'Over 13 crore voters deleted.' PTI-Bhasha's Hindi (dk-bhasha): ''वर्ष 2024 में जीत का अंतर सिर्फ दो प्रतिशत था। तेरह करोड़ से ज़्यादा मतदाताओं के नाम हटा दिए गए।'' which is the agency's translation. In what language he said it is not known. Business Today (24 September) reports him calling the 2 per cent 'the NDA-opposition gap'.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's state-by-state counts of names left off the draft rolls, and the 2024 Lok Sabha vote shares of the two alliances.
claims.check: The count holds to the precision he gives. Across the 31 states and union territories with a draft, 13,39,03,307 names were left off, 14.08 per 100 on the rolls before, which is his 'over 13 crore' and 'around 14 percent'. The word 'deleted' does not fit them. These are names not carried into the drafts, with reasons officers recorded, and they include the dead and duplicate entries. In the 22 states with a final roll, part came back. The '2 per cent' is not checked by the site. PTI itself puts the NDA at around 43 per cent of the 2024 vote and the INDIA bloc parties at around 40.6 per cent, a gap of about 2.4 points, but the site holds no national party vote shares and has not checked those figures against the Commission's statistical report. The two percentages also have different bases: 2 per cent is of votes cast, 14 per cent of names on the roll.
claims.site_counts: 13,39,03,307 names left off the drafts in 31 states, of 95,08,13,771 on the rolls before: 14.08 per 100 (data/india/states.json, total.removed, total.per_100). By recorded reason, 2,79,69,558 dead (20.9%), 9,56,35,923 shifted, absent or other (71.5%), 1,01,48,459 duplicate (7.6%) (total.shares). In the 22 states with a final roll, 7,77,48,303 were left off of 65,67,36,949 (11.84 per 100), and the net fall from the roll before to the final roll was 6,63,72,065 (10.11 per 100). The rise after the draft made up at most 14.6% of the names left off (states.json, final.per_100, final.net_per_100, final.made_up_pct; recomputed from the 22 rows with electors_final). The 13,39,03,307 equal 21.8 per 100 votes cast in those 31 states in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, 61,45,74,272 votes (data/india/raw/adults_ls2024.csv, votes_2024; states.json, removed_pct_votes24).
claims.site_stops: A reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it. Nine states have no final roll yet, so the 13 crore is still mostly a draft figure (states.json, final.waiting). The site counts names and cannot say how many of those left off were eligible electors, or how many would have voted.

claims.quote: Where 2 per cent is deciding the election, you are deleting 13 crore votes. What is this if not a setting?
claims.speaker_note: PTI's evening copy, ETV Bharat and National Herald end with a question mark; PTI's afternoon copy ends 'setting,” he asked.' PTI-Bhasha: ''जहां दो प्रतिशत वोट परिणाम तय कर रहे हों, वहां आप 13 करोड़ वोट हटा रहे हैं। अगर यह 'मिलीभगत' नहीं है, तो फिर क्या है?'' PTI's own lead says he 'accused the government of attempting to influence electoral outcomes through alleged voter deletions'. At the same press conference Aishe Ghosh said 'Gyanesh has helped them win the whole country' and Neha Bora 'When you drag common people, you are dragging those 13 crore people' (PTI).
claims.relies_on: The size of the names left off set against a national vote-share gap from 2024.
claims.check: 'Setting' is a claim about purpose, and the rolls cannot show purpose either way. The comparison under it does not hold as stated. The 2024 Lok Sabha election was held on the rolls before the revision, which the Commission ordered on 24 June 2025, so nothing left off in the SIR could have touched the 2024 result. A national vote-share gap does not decide an election under first past the post, seat margins do. Measured by seats, the site finds names left off large against close margins: spread evenly over each state's Lok Sabha seats, they exceed the 2024 margin in 373 of 516 seats, and 115 of the 542 contested seats were won by under 50,000 votes. The one place the site estimates an effect on a result is Bihar. There the names left off came more from booths that had voted NDA in 2024, and the estimates have 4 to 6 seats changing hands, in both directions, with no change in which alliance holds a majority.
claims.site_counts: The revision was ordered on 24 June 2025, starting with Bihar (data/india/process.json, timeline). 2024 Lok Sabha seats won by under 50,000 votes: 115, and under 1,00,000: 232, of 542 contested (data/india/margins.json, ls_close). With each state's names left off spread evenly over its Lok Sabha seats, more than the 2024 margin in 373 of 516 seats in 31 states (margins.json, even_total). That spread is an assumption: in Tamil Nadu it gives 27 seats over the margin against 19 counted from constituency tables, in Bihar 32 against 32 (margins.json, even_test). Bihar: those removed came from booths that voted 49.0% NDA and 37.8% INDIA in 2024; on the booth estimate 4 seats change hands on the low count (1 to the NDA, 3 to the INDIA bloc) and 6 on the high count (3 each way) (data/bihar/impact.json, comp_booth_all, summary.booth_lower, summary.booth_upper).
claims.site_stops: The rolls record names and reasons. They cannot show why the revision was run as it was, and no page of the site says what anyone intended. Over the margin means the names left off were large enough to decide a seat, never that they did. The site has no national vote shares and does not model a Lok Sabha election on the revised rolls, which has not been held.

claims.quote: In total, more than 13 crore votes have been deleted. This is not a small number.
claims.speaker_note: His press conference of 24 September 2026, as Business Today quotes it. Business Today adds, in its own words, that more than 13 crore names had then been struck off the drafts across 30 states and union territories.
claims.relies_on: The Commission's draft-roll figures.
claims.check: The number holds and has grown a little since: 13,39,03,307 across 31 states as of 13 October 2026. It counts names, and calling them votes or deletions goes beyond what it is: names left off the drafts, by reasons officers recorded, some since restored.

claims.quote: Pinarayi Vijayan would have won, but due to the deletion of votes in Kerala, he did not become the Chief Minister.
claims.speaker_note: As Business Today quotes him on 24 September 2026. Business Today adds that he gave no evidence that the deletions decided the Kerala outcome.
claims.relies_on: The fall in Kerala's roll during the revision.
claims.check: The site's figures do not carry the claim that far. Kerala published no count of names left off. The roll fell by 23,68,590 from January 2025 to the draft, but rose again after it, and by the 2026 election the fall was 6,67,990, 2.40 per 100. That fall exceeded the winning margin in 38 of the 140 seats, 30 when taken at each seat's turnout. In Vijayan's own seat, Dharmadam, the roll at the election was larger than in January 2025, and the CPI(M) held it by 19,247. Whether the names left off would have changed which front formed the government cannot be read from the rolls.
claims.site_counts: Kerala: roll of January 2025 2,78,10,942, draft 2,54,42,352, roll at the 2026 election 2,71,42,952. Fall to the draft 23,68,590 (8.52 per 100), fall to the election roll 6,67,990 (2.40 per 100). The fall exceeded the margin in 38 of 140 seats, and in 30 at the seat's turnout. Seats won in 2026: INC 63, CPI(M) 26, IUML 22, CPI 8 and others (data/kerala/summary.json). claims.site_stops: Kerala's measure is the fall in the roll, which takes in ordinary changes and new voters, and is never called the names removed. Over the margin means large enough to decide a seat, never that it did.

strongest_points: His count is right to the precision he gives: 13,39,03,307 names were left off the drafts, 14.08 per 100 on the rolls before.

The names left off are large against close seat margins. Spread evenly, they exceed the 2024 Lok Sabha margin in 373 of 516 seats in the 31 states, and they equal 21.8 per 100 of the votes those states cast in 2024.
overreach: The 2024 election was held on the rolls before the revision, so the names left off in the SIR could not have decided it.
'Deleted' overstates what the 13 crore are: names left off the drafts by recorded reason, including the dead and duplicate entries, part of which came back on the final rolls.
A national vote-share gap is the wrong yardstick for a Lok Sabha result, which is decided seat by seat, and it is a share of votes set against a share of names on the roll.
'Setting' is a claim of intent the rolls cannot show. In Bihar, the one state where the site estimates an effect on seats, the estimate is 4 to 6 seats changing hands in both directions.
The Kerala claim goes further than the fall in the roll, which by election day was 2.40 per 100 and exceeded the margin in 38 of 140 seats.
